lines: Well, hello there, neighbour! I'm Mr. Palmer. I look after things round here. Town meetings, the gazebo, that sort of thing.
{player}: Mr. Palmer?! You look just like the mayor of Galaxity!
(Mr. Palmer looks left. Then right. Then he leans down and whispers.)
Shh! Nobody here knows about that. On this side of the portal I'm just plain old Mr. Palmer.
Lots of us have a Galaxity side, you know. You look a bit different over there yourself, I expect.
{player}: I do?
Everyone does! That's the fun of it.
(Mr. Palmer jumps.) Oh! Goodness! {player}! Just... admiring the old oak. Lovely tree. Lovely bark.
{player}: At midnight?
Best time for it! It hums a bit this time of night, doesn't it? (He winks.) Off you go, then. And mind you're home by one.
Morning, neighbour! Tea on the porch. Best way to start the day. Well, second best. The first is not losing the string lights.
Lunch at the diner. Gus pretends he doesn't save me the window seat. He saves me the window seat.
Town business! Today: should the gazebo be painted white, or a slightly different white? Very important.
Oh dear, oh dear. The autumn festival's coming, and I've lost the string lights for the gazebo!
Three boxes of them. I put them down somewhere on my way round the green... by the diner? The bookshop? The inn?
Would you? You're a star. Just like back home, eh?
No rush. You live just round the corner, after all.
No rush. The festival can wait. The gazebo's very patient.
Any luck with those lights? By the diner, the bookshop or the inn, I'm sure of it. Fairly sure. A bit sure.
{player}: Mr. Palmer! I found all three boxes!
You found them! Splendid! Let's get them up.
(Mr. Palmer strings the lights round the gazebo roof. {player} holds the ladder. Click!)
(The gazebo glows warm and golden. A few people on the green stop to say ooh.)
There. Now it's a proper autumn evening.
Come by tomorrow and you can help with the festival. There's apple pie and hot apple juice.

rotate: Doesn't the gazebo look lovely? I keep walking past it just to look.
Off through the portal again tonight? Say hello to my other side for me.
Lovely evening for it. Autumn's my favourite. Everything smells like leaves.
The portal by the old oak opens at midnight. But you didn't hear that from me.
